outcome: Since 26 January 2024 nothing has resolved the conjecture as stated; two preprints prove the Poisson pair-correlation prediction for restricted classes of integrable quantum systems (Kim–Marklof–Welsh, arXiv 2601.03209, 6 Jan 2026, quantum particle in a 3D box with Diophantine side ratios; Lutsko, arXiv 2609.03112, 2 Sep 2026, three-particle Sutherland model at Diophantine coupling), and the Lutsko preprint's own AI-use declaration names ChatGPT (OpenAI) as used in developing and checking preliminary proof strategies.
problem_asks: The Wikipedia entry is terse ('Berry–Tabor conjecture in quantum chaos'), so the parts below are read from the conjecture as the cited sources state it (Berry and Tabor 1977; Wikipedia's Quantum chaos article: when the classical dynamics is completely integrable, the quantum energy eigenvalues behave like independent random variables). (1) For quantum systems whose classical counterpart is integrable, the local statistics of the energy eigenvalues (semiclassical limit, after unfolding) are those of a Poisson point process. (2) The claim is for generic integrable systems: the 'generic' qualifier is part of the assertion, so non-generic integrable systems (the harmonic oscillator, geodesic flow on the sphere or other Zoll surfaces, the Haldane–Shastry chain) fall outside it. (3) 'Local statistics' is not fixed by the statement. It covers the pair-correlation (two-point) measure, the nearest-neighbour spacing distribution, and higher n-point correlations. The sources treat these as separate statistics that need not imply one another.

events.what_happened: Peter Sarnak proved the Berry–Tabor pair-correlation statement for almost every flat 2-torus (equivalently, almost all positive definite binary quadratic forms, 'almost all' in Lebesgue measure on the moduli space), by averaging and a Borel–Cantelli-type argument. Written up in 'Arithmetic quantum chaos', The Schur Lectures (1992), Israel Math. Conf. Proc. 8 (1995), pp. 183–236; an IAS listing dates the lectures to May 1993. Reported second-hand as the first proof in Marklof (2003) and Eskin–Margulis–Mozes (2005). The Sarnak text itself was not opened, and the year of the first written proof is not confirmed.
events.delivers: Poisson pair correlation of the eigenvalues of the flat-torus Laplacian for almost every flat 2-torus (Lebesgue-almost every point of the moduli space). Restricted to 2-tori, to the pair-correlation statistic, and to a full-measure set of tori. Secondary sources add that the conjecture fails on a set of second Baire category of tori (not verified).
events.remains: Every torus outside the full-measure set; the spacing distribution and higher correlations; the general statement for generic integrable systems.

checked_by.who: Jens Marklof (2003) and Alex Eskin, Gregory Margulis, Shahar Mozes (2005)
checked_by.qualification: Specialists in this area who restate the result as known in the introductions of their own papers
checked_by.what_they_did: Cite and restate Sarnak's theorem as established; not an independent verification (read via search snippets)

events.direction: Confirms the Berry–Tabor prediction on the Poisson side, but only for almost every torus. The same secondary sources report a second-category set of tori where the pair-correlation limit fails, which is the 'generic' caveat in another form.

events.what_happened: Jens Marklof, 'Pair correlation densities of inhomogeneous quadratic forms', arXiv math/0210197, posted 14 Oct 2002 (v2, 20 Apr 2004, the published version, 53 pages); Annals of Mathematics 158 (2003), 419–471. Shows that under explicit Diophantine conditions on (α, β) the local two-point correlations of the values (m−α)²+(n−β)² over Z² are those of a Poisson process. The Annals abstract says this 'partly confirms a conjecture of Berry and Tabor'. Also proves a special case of the quantitative Oppenheim conjecture for signature (2,2) inhomogeneous forms. Method: theta sums and Ratner's classification of unipotent-invariant measures.
events.revisions: v1 14 Oct 2002; v2 20 Apr 2004 (published version, 53 pages); Annals 158 (2003), 419–471.
events.delivers: Poisson two-point (pair correlation) statistics for the sequence (m−α)²+(n−β)² over Z² under explicit Diophantine conditions on (α, β). Two-dimensional, inhomogeneous, two-point statistic only. Its values can be read as Laplace eigenvalues of a flat torus with quasi-periodic boundary conditions (secondary summary).
events.remains: Pairs (α, β) outside the Diophantine class (the abstract says the theorem does not cover all real pairs); the spacing distribution; higher correlations; the general conjecture for generic integrable systems.

checked_by.who: Editors and referees of Annals of Mathematics
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper, Annals 158 (2003), 419–471

events.direction: Confirms the Berry–Tabor prediction on the Poisson side for a two-dimensional inhomogeneous family; the author calls the confirmation partial.

events.what_happened: Jens Marklof, 'Pair correlation densities of inhomogeneous quadratic forms II', arXiv math/0210198, posted 14 Oct 2002 (single version, no journal reference on the arXiv page). Shows that the local pair-correlation density of the values ||m−α||^k for m in Z^k is Poisson under Diophantine conditions on α: for k = 2 any Diophantine type works; for k > 2 only Diophantine types κ < (k−1)/(k−2). Presented as supporting the Berry–Tabor conjecture. A 2026 bibliography labels this paper 'Duke'; that is not verified.
events.delivers: Poisson pair correlation of ||m−α||^k over m in Z^k for Diophantine vectors α; in dimension k = 2 for every Diophantine type; in k > 2 only for types κ < (k−1)/(k−2). Two-point statistic only.
events.remains: Vectors α outside these types; all α when k > 2; the spacing distribution and higher correlations; the general conjecture.
events.direction: Supports the Poisson side of Berry–Tabor for this family; partial and dimension-dependent.

events.what_happened: Steve Zelditch, 'Level spacings for integrable quantum maps in genus zero', Comm. Math. Phys. 196 (1998), 289–318; arXiv math-ph/0002010 posted 4 Feb 2000, with addendum math-ph/0002011. For quantizations of time-one maps of integrable Hamiltonian flows on the 2-sphere (acting on homogeneous polynomials of degree N), proves that for almost all members of a broad two-parameter family of Hamiltonians the limiting pair correlation of eigenphase spacings is Poisson, along a slightly sparse subsequence of N. The addendum extends this with Cesàro means over the full sequence. The abstract describes the result as a weaker version of the Berry–Tabor conjecture.
events.revisions: Journal publication 1998 (CMP 196); arXiv math-ph/0002010 posted 4 Feb 2000; addendum math-ph/0002011.
events.delivers: Poisson pair correlation of eigenphase spacings for almost every member of one two-parameter family of integrable quantum maps on the sphere, along a sparse subsequence (main theorem) and in Cesàro mean (addendum). Restricted to a.e. member of a family, to quantum maps on S² rather than the problem's Hamiltonians, and to pair correlation.
events.remains: Members of the family outside the a.e. set; every other statistic; quantum Hamiltonians in general; the full sequence of N in the main theorem (addendum handles the mean).

checked_by.who: Referees and editors of Communications in Mathematical Physics
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper in 1998

events.doubts: The author calls the result a weaker form of the conjecture, and the main theorem uses a sparse subsequence of N; the addendum removes this with Cesàro means. These are the author's own scope limits.
events.direction: Confirms the Poisson prediction for almost every member of a family of integrable quantum maps; a weakened form of the conjecture, not its statement.

events.what_happened: Steve Zelditch and Maciej Zworski, 'Spacings between phase shifts in a simple scattering problem', Comm. Math. Phys. 204 (1999), 709–729, DOI 10.1007/s002200050663; arXiv math-ph/0002006 posted 3 Feb 2000 (single version). Scattering-theory version of the Berry–Tabor idea (the analogous conjecture of Smilansky): for almost every surface in a class of cylindrical surfaces of revolution with a conic singularity, the large-energy limit of the pair correlation measure of quantum phase shifts is the uniform (Poisson) measure.
events.revisions: Journal publication 1999 (CMP 204); arXiv math-ph/0002006 posted 3 Feb 2000, one version.
events.delivers: Poisson pair correlation of quantum phase shifts (scattering matrix eigenphases) for almost every surface in one class of surfaces of revolution with a cylindrical end. This is an open-system scattering quantity, not the bound-state spectrum of a closed integrable Hamiltonian.
events.remains: Bound-state spectra and closed integrable Hamiltonians; surfaces outside the a.e. class; every other statistic.

checked_by.who: Referees and editors of Communications in Mathematical Physics
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper in 1999

events.doubts: A search snippet describes the result as covering a 2-parameter family with full measure; the arXiv abstract says 'a class of cylindrical surfaces of revolution' and the snippet's 'infinite-dimensional family' wording conflicts with it. The abstract is recorded here; the conflict is not resolved.
events.direction: Supports the scattering analogue of the Poisson prediction for almost every surface in one class. Not a case of the closed-system conjecture as stated.

events.what_happened: Jens Marklof, 'Spectral form factors of rectangle billiards', mp_arc 98-61 (16 Feb 1998); Comm. Math. Phys. 199 (1998), 169–202. For a rectangle billiard with random side ratio, the sum over eigenvalues of exp(2πiλ_j τ) (τ random, N large) behaves like a random walk with a non-Gaussian limit law. The variance, 'essentially the average pair correlation function', equals one, in accordance with the Berry–Tabor conjecture, but all moments of order four and above diverge. Proof uses mixing on a product of hyperbolic surfaces. The abstract says the Berry–Tabor conjecture and the limit law for a fixed generic rectangle are tied to an equidistribution conjecture for long horocycles.
events.revisions: mp_arc 98-61 (16 Feb 1998); journal Comm. Math. Phys. 199 (1998), 169–202.
events.delivers: For a rectangle with random side ratio: the variance of the limit law (the average pair correlation) equals one, consistent with Berry–Tabor; the limit law exists and is non-Gaussian; moments of order four and above diverge. The statistic is a random exponential sum, not the spacing distribution, and only its variance matches the prediction.
events.remains: The Poisson limit of local statistics for a fixed generic rectangle (tied to a horocycle equidistribution conjecture); the spacing distribution; higher correlations; the general conjecture.

checked_by.who: Referees and editors of Communications in Mathematical Physics
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper in 1998

events.direction: Agrees with the Poisson prediction only in the variance; higher moments diverge, so this is consistent with the conjecture but does not prove the Poisson law for a fixed rectangle.

events.what_happened: VanderKam is credited with extending Sarnak's almost-everywhere pair-correlation result to generic flat 4-tori, using an unfolding procedure. A 2026 preprint cites VanderKam works Van99a, Van99b and Van00, and attributes to Van00 convergence to the Poissonian k-point correlation measure for d ≥ 2k. The original paper was not found, so its title, journal and year are unverified. The citation keys suggest 1999 or 2000.
events.delivers: Pair correlation of Laplace eigenvalues Poisson for almost every (generic) flat 4-torus, per secondary sources; the 2026 preprint attributes k-point Poisson convergence for d ≥ 2k to Van00. Unverified.
events.remains: Non-generic 4-tori; the spacing distribution; the general conjecture.
events.direction: Supports the Poisson prediction for almost every 4-torus, if the secondary description is right. Not verified against the original.
people: VanderKam (first name and initials not found)

events.what_happened: Alex Eskin, Gregory Margulis, Shahar Mozes, 'Quadratic forms of signature (2,2) and eigenvalue spacings on rectangular 2-tori', Annals of Mathematics 161 (2005), 679–725 (DOI 10.4007/annals.2005.161.679). Gives explicit Diophantine conditions under which the eigenvalue pair correlations (spacings) of rectangular 2-tori are Poissonian, via an asymptotic counting theorem for integer points on irrational (2,2) forms. The Annals page has no abstract and was received 28 Feb 2001 and accepted 29 Jun 2003. The statement above comes from secondary summaries (Margulis–Mohammadi 2010, search snippets). No preprint was found, so the first public date may be earlier than 2005.
events.revisions: No preprint found. Annals 161 (2005), 679–725; received 28 Feb 2001, accepted 29 Jun 2003 per the journal page.
events.delivers: Poisson pair correlation of eigenvalues on rectangular 2-tori for parameters satisfying explicit Diophantine conditions (secondary summary). Restricted to rectangular 2-tori, to the Diophantine parameter set, and to the two-point statistic.
events.remains: Parameters outside the Diophantine set; non-rectangular tori; higher correlations and spacing distributions; the general conjecture (the 2026 Kim–Marklof–Welsh paper extends this to 3-boxes).

checked_by.who: Referees and editors of Annals of Mathematics
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper, Annals 161 (2005)

events.direction: Confirms the Poisson prediction for specific rectangular 2-tori under Diophantine parameter conditions; partial.

events.what_happened: J.C. Barba, F. Finkel, A. Gonzalez-Lopez, M.A. Rodriguez, 'The Berry–Tabor conjecture for spin chains of Haldane–Shastry type', arXiv 0804.3685 (23 Apr 2008); Europhys. Lett. 83 (2008) 27005. Finds that the level-spacing distribution of the integrable Haldane–Shastry spin chain (long-range interactions) is neither Poisson nor Wigner-type. Proposes a 'square root of a logarithm' cumulative spacing law for the family and verifies it for Polychronakos's rational counterpart. The paper calls the chain 'an important exception to the Berry–Tabor conjecture'.
events.delivers: A non-Poisson level-spacing law for one integrable spin chain (Haldane–Shastry) and its rational relative (Polychronakos), proposed as a feature of the family. Relevant to the 'generic' qualifier: it is a counterexample to Poisson spacing for an integrable model, not a disproof of the generic statement.
events.remains: Nothing about the generic statement is settled either way; whether the chain is excluded by 'generic' is a judging question. The paper treats the chain as an exception.

checked_by.who: Referees and editors of Europhysics Letters
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper, EPL 83 (2008) 27005

events.direction: Against the Poisson prediction for this specific integrable model (the authors call it an exception). Whether the model is 'generic' is for the judging pass.

events.what_happened: Jens Marklof and Nadav Yesha, 'Pair correlation for quadratic polynomials mod 1', arXiv 1701.09163 (31 Jan 2017; revised 24 Mar 2017 and 14 Nov 2017); Compositio Math. 154 (2018), 960–983. Gives explicit Diophantine conditions on the coefficients of degree-two polynomials under which an averaged pair-correlation density of the fractional parts of the polynomial values at integers converges to the Poisson limit. The abstract says these polynomials give the energy levels of certain integrable quantum systems and that the findings 'provide further evidence for the Berry–Tabor conjecture in the theory of quantum chaos'.
events.delivers: Poisson (averaged) pair correlation of the fractional parts of degree-two polynomial values at integers, under explicit Diophantine conditions on the coefficients. The abstract links this to integrable quantum energy levels; the authors state it as further evidence rather than a proof of the quantum statement. Averaged, two-point, sequence-level.
events.remains: Coefficients outside the Diophantine conditions; the quantum systems in general; the non-averaged statement; spacing and higher correlations; the general conjecture.

checked_by.who: Referees and editors of Compositio Mathematica
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper, Compositio 154 (2018)

events.direction: Supports the Poisson prediction for a sequence that the authors say models integrable quantum energy levels. Whether that sequence is a case of the statement is the judging pass's call; I record it as an analogue.

events.what_happened: N. Minami, 'On level clustering in regular spectra', mp_arc 00-171 (7 Apr 2000), an expository elaboration of an earlier note (mp_arc 00-163, not opened). Gives a mathematical formulation of the Berry–Tabor level-clustering idea. Defines strict and wide sense level clustering and proves preliminary propositions, by analogy with stationary point processes. Argues that strict-sense clustering for generic regular spectra is probably very hard to prove from Sinai–Major theorems, while wide-sense clustering might be provable for a concrete Hamiltonian such as the rectangular billiard. Concludes that 'level clustering' should not always mean strict Poissonian property of the spectrum.
events.delivers: No theorem about the Poisson statistics of any particular integrable spectrum. It reformulates the conjecture as strict or wide-sense level clustering and proves preliminary properties of these notions. Shows that the conjecture's wording admits a weaker reading.
events.remains: Everything: no integrable spectrum is shown to cluster in either sense in this paper.
events.direction: Neutral on the outcome; sharpens what the conjecture asserts, and argues that the strict version is hard to reach.

events.what_happened: Valentin Blomer and Maksym Radziwiłł, 'Small gaps in the spectrum of tori: asymptotic formulae', arXiv 2108.11162 (25 Aug 2021, single version). Asymptotic formula for the number of pairs of neighbouring Laplace eigenvalues on flat tori that are unusually close (small gaps) among the first N eigenvalues, for almost all flat tori and almost all rectangular flat tori, valid down to the Planck scale. A Springer DOI (10.1007/s00220-023-04760-3) appears in search results; the page redirected to a login, so the journal and year are unverified.
events.delivers: An asymptotic count of small gaps among the first N eigenvalues for almost all flat tori. A gap statistic on the same spectra, not the pair-correlation or spacing limit. A secondary source says the count matches what a Poisson spacing law predicts for generic tori (not verified).
events.remains: The pair-correlation and spacing limits as such; non-generic tori; the general conjecture.
events.doubts: A search snippet describes the paper as keyed to the Berry–Tabor conjecture; the arXiv abstract page does not mention it. The abstract is recorded here; the discrepancy is not resolved.
events.direction: A neighbouring gap statistic on almost all tori, consistent with a Poisson picture. Not a statement about the pair-correlation or spacing limit.

events.what_happened: Christoph Aistleitner, Valentin Blomer, Maksym Radziwiłł, 'Triple correlation and long gaps in the spectrum of flat tori', arXiv 1809.07881 (20 Sep 2018, single version). Computes an averaged triple correlation of Laplace eigenvalues on generic flat tori: almost surely the liminf is at most Poissonian and the limsup at least Poissonian. Consequence: almost all flat tori have infinitely many spectral gaps at least 2.006 times the mean gap. Also constructs sequences with Poisson pair correlation and consecutive spacings bounded by 2. A search snippet (not verified) reports publication in J. Eur. Math. Soc. in 2024 and says the Berry–Tabor conjecture for generic flat tori 'remains wide open'.
events.revisions: v1 only on arXiv. JEMS publication reported in snippets only, not verified.
events.delivers: An almost-sure averaged triple-correlation statement and a long-gap statement for generic flat tori. Not the pair-correlation or spacing limit for any individual torus. The sequence construction does not concern tori.
events.remains: Pair-correlation and spacing Poisson limits for individual or generic tori; the general conjecture.
events.direction: Partial, neighbouring statistics; supports Poissonian behaviour in an averaged higher-correlation sense, not the two-point or spacing statement.

events.what_happened: Jens Marklof and Laura Monk, 'The moduli space of twisted Laplacians and random matrix theory', arXiv 2407.10778 (submitted 15 Jul 2024; v2 4 Oct 2024; comments say 'to appear in IMRN'). Extends Rudnick's number-variance approach: averaged over Weil–Petersson moduli space for large compact hyperbolic surfaces, twisted Laplacians that break time-reversal symmetry converge to GUE number variance, and Dirac operators to GSE, in a scaling limit. Answers a question of Naud. Not a Poisson result: this is the chaotic, random-matrix side of the Bohigas–Giannoni–Schmit picture.
events.revisions: v1 15 Jul 2024; v2 4 Oct 2024 (to appear IMRN per comments).
events.delivers: Random-matrix number-variance limits (GUE for twisted Laplacians, GSE for Dirac operators) on compact hyperbolic surfaces averaged over moduli. Chaotic side only; it does not touch the Poisson prediction.
events.remains: Everything bearing on the Berry–Tabor (integrable, Poisson) statement.
events.direction: Different question (the chaotic / random-matrix side of Bohigas–Giannoni–Schmit). Does not bear on the Poisson prediction. Possibly the Monk-coauthored result named in the 21 Oct 2025 Oxford talk; not confirmed.

events.what_happened: Wooyeon Kim, Jens Marklof, Matthew Welsh, 'Values of ternary quadratic forms at integers and the Berry–Tabor conjecture for 3-tori', arXiv 2601.03209 (math.NT; also math-ph and math.DS), v1 submitted 6 Jan 2026 by Welsh; 29 pages. No later version and no journal reference found as of 10 Oct 2026. Verifies the Berry–Tabor two-point spectral density (pair correlation measure) for a quantum particle in a three-dimensional box (Dirichlet Laplacian) when the squared side-length ratios are κ-Diophantine for κ close to 1 (Theorem 1.1; abstract example ratios 1, 2^(1/3), 2^(−1/3)). Extends Eskin–Margulis–Mozes (2005) from dimension two. Method: counting values of ternary forms over shrinking intervals, written as an average of a theta function over unipotent orbits; Ratner's measure classification and escape-of-mass estimates; special diagonal (3,3) forms. Introduction: 'there is currently no complete proof of either phenomenon for a single example.'
events.delivers: Poissonian pair-correlation measure of the rescaled eigenvalues of a three-dimensional box whose squared side-length ratios are κ-Diophantine for κ near 1. Two-point statistic only; one quantum particle in a box; the Diophantine ratio class (the authors note the statement fails for all rational length ratios, where the two-point measure diverges).
events.remains: The spacing distribution ('appears to be equally difficult'); triple and higher correlations ('much less understood in the deterministic setting'); boxes outside the Diophantine class; d ≥ 4 (expected under Diophantine conditions, not proved); other integrable systems and the generic statement. The authors say the Diophantine conditions 'are likely not sharp'.
events.direction: Cuts for the conjecture: verifies the Poisson pair-correlation prediction for a restricted class of integrable systems (3D boxes with Diophantine side ratios). Does not establish the generic statement, which the authors say has no complete proof for a single example.

events.what_happened: Chris Lutsko, Nick Rome, Niclas Technau, 'Poissonian correlations of αn^d mod 1', arXiv 2605.06974 (v1 7 May 2026; v2 13 May 2026). For the sequence αn^d mod 1 (d > 1 an integer, α nonzero real): Poissonian ℓ-point correlations for almost all α when d is large relative to ℓ; and, following a Rudnick–Sarnak conjecture, for a set of badly approximable α of full Hausdorff dimension, via a Fourier transference principle and determinant-method point counts. Abstract: 'This falls in line with the expected behavior from the Berry--Tabor conjecture.' The introduction calls the result 'almost everywhere evidence towards the Berry–Tabor conjecture'. The reference list cites KMW (ref [17]).
events.delivers: Poissonian ℓ-point correlations for the sequence αn^d mod 1 for almost all α when d is large relative to ℓ, and for badly approximable α of full dimension. A number-theoretic sequence, not a quantum system or spectrum.
events.remains: Every statement about quantum spectra; the conjecture as stated; small d.
events.direction: An analogue of the Poisson prediction for a different sequence. The authors say it is consistent with Berry–Tabor; it is not about a quantum system.

events.what_happened: Christopher Lutsko (sole author), 'Poissonian pair correlations for the three-particle Sutherland model', arXiv 2609.03112 (v1 only, 2 Sep 2026; 13 pages; math.NT, math-ph). For the repulsive three-particle trigonometric Sutherland Hamiltonian (coupling g > 1), at fixed total momentum K in Z, the desymmetrized spectrum has Poissonian pair correlation when g is Diophantine of finite type (Theorem 1). The proof reduces to a finite-congruence, Weyl-sector version of Marklof's theorem on inhomogeneous quadratic forms. The author writes: 'To our knowledge, Theorem 1 is the first rigorous proof of Poissonian pair correlation for a deterministic quantum Hamiltonian with multiple interacting particles.' The AI-use declaration names ChatGPT (see ai).
events.delivers: Poisson pair correlation (only that statistic) for the desymmetrized spectrum of the three-particle Sutherland Hamiltonian, for Diophantine finite-type coupling g > 1 and any integer total momentum K. Restricted to N = 3 particles, to the pair-correlation statistic, and to Diophantine couplings.
events.remains: N ≥ 4 particles ('For N≥4 this creates additional collisions', Remark 2); non-Diophantine couplings ('irrationality alone is not enough for the present proof', Remark 11; Section 1 says 'Some Diophantine restriction is necessary in general'); the spacing distribution and higher correlations; generic integrable systems in general; the conjecture as stated.
events.directly_checkable: The relative spectrum is said to be a translate of a positive-definite A2 quadratic form at fixed total momentum, so the reduction is in principle checkable by hand. No public check found. The author's acknowledgement thanks Jens Marklof for comments on an earlier draft; that is private comment, not a public check.
events.doubts: (1) Per the AI declaration, ChatGPT was used in developing and checking preliminary proof strategies; the paper does not say which steps. The author states that all arguments were independently evaluated and verified by the author. Single author, unrefereed, no public engagement found. (2) The priority claim ('first rigorous proof ... for a deterministic quantum Hamiltonian with multiple interacting particles', hedged 'to our knowledge') sits next to earlier rigorous Poisson pair-correlation results for deterministic quantum Hamiltonians (Eskin–Margulis–Mozes 2005 on rectangular 2-tori; Kim–Marklof–Welsh 2026 on 3D boxes). Whether 'multiple interacting particles' carries the claim is a scope question. See disputes.
events.direction: Cuts for the conjecture: verifies the Poisson pair-correlation prediction for one three-particle integrable model at Diophantine coupling. Does not settle the general generic statement.

systems.name: ChatGPT (OpenAI)
systems.what_it_did: Per the authors' AI-use declaration: 'used in developing and checking preliminary proof strategies, verifying calculations and logical consistency, revising the exposition, checking bibliographic information, and assisting with LaTeX preparation.' The declaration does not say which proof step, if any, the tool originated. The only sentence that could reach the main argument is 'developing ... preliminary proof strategies'. The source names a product, not a model version.
systems.basis_quote: Generative artificial intelligence, ChatGPT (OpenAI), was used in developing and checking preliminary proof strategies, verifying calculations and logical consistency, revising the exposition, checking bibliographic information, and assisting with LaTeX preparation. All mathematical arguments, statements, and citations in the final manuscript were independently evaluated and verified by the author. The author made every final decision concerning the content and assumes full responsibility for the correctness and originality of the paper.

disputes.summary: Lutsko (2 Sep 2026) claims to be the first rigorous proof of Poissonian pair correlation for a deterministic quantum Hamiltonian with multiple interacting particles. Earlier rigorous Poisson pair-correlation results for deterministic quantum Hamiltonians include Eskin–Margulis–Mozes (2005, rectangular 2-tori), Marklof (1998 and 2003), and Kim–Marklof–Welsh (6 Jan 2026, a single particle in a 3D box). Whether the qualifier 'with multiple interacting particles' makes the claim true is not resolved here; the record leaves it to the judging pass.
Blomer–Radziwiłł (2021): a search snippet says the paper is keyed to the Berry–Tabor conjecture; the arXiv abstract page does not mention it. Not resolved.

Zelditch–Zworski (1999/2000): a search snippet describes a full-measure set in a 2-parameter family, and elsewhere an 'infinite-dimensional family'; the arXiv abstract says 'a class of cylindrical surfaces of revolution'. The abstract is recorded; not resolved.

summary: The statement is the Berry–Tabor conjecture (1977): generic integrable quantum systems have Poisson local eigenvalue statistics. Nothing in the window from 26 January 2024 to 10 October 2026 resolves it. Two post-window preprints verify the pair-correlation (two-point) prediction for restricted classes. Kim–Marklof–Welsh (arXiv 2601.03209, 6 Jan 2026) treat a quantum particle in a 3D box whose squared side ratios are κ-Diophantine, extending Eskin–Margulis–Mozes from dimension two; the authors state that there is 'currently no complete proof of either phenomenon for a single example.' Lutsko (arXiv 2609.03112, 2 Sep 2026) treats the three-particle Sutherland model at a Diophantine finite-type coupling, with the claim 'to our knowledge' of being the first rigorous proof of this kind for a deterministic quantum Hamiltonian with several interacting particles. Lutsko is the only AI-involved item I found. Its AI-use declaration says 'Generative artificial intelligence, ChatGPT (OpenAI), was used in developing and checking preliminary proof strategies,' and also for verifying calculations, revising the exposition, checking bibliography and LaTeX; it adds that the author independently verified all arguments. The declaration does not say which proof step came from the tool. This is a close call: read narrowly, the mention is ancillary to a reduction the abstract credits to Marklof's theorem; read broadly, 'proof strategies' reaches the core argument. I record it and leave the weighing to the judging pass. The Kim–Marklof–Welsh full text has no AI, LLM, software or computer-assisted statement. The May 2026 Lutsko–Rome–Technau preprint (arXiv 2605.06974) is an analogue for the sequence αn^d mod 1, which its authors say 'falls in line with' Berry–Tabor; it has no AI declaration and I record it as discarded. Earlier partial results are substantial and are recorded as separate events: Sarnak (almost every flat 2-torus; the year is only confirmed to the volume, 1995); Marklof 2002/2003 (inhomogeneous binary forms, 'partly confirms'); Zelditch 1998 and Zelditch–Zworski 1999 (a.e. integrable quantum maps and a scattering analogue); Marklof 1998 (rectangle billiard: variance one, higher moments diverge); Eskin–Margulis–Mozes (Annals 2005, rectangular 2-tori); VanderKam (a.e. 4-tori; original not found); and Barba et al. (2008), who call the Haldane–Shastry chain 'an important exception' to the conjecture. Neighbouring statistics are Aistleitner–Blomer–Radziwiłł (2018, triple correlation and long gaps) and Blomer–Radziwiłł (2021, small gaps). Marklof–Monk (2024) is on the random-matrix side and does not bear on the Poisson prediction. The Oxford talk of 21 Oct 2025 names a result 'obtained in collaboration with Laura Monk' as one of its two most recent; I could not locate it, and it is listed under incomplete. The Wikipedia list entry links to a section of the Quantum chaos article, not to a dedicated article; that article calls the conjecture 'still open'. No retraction, objection, Lean formalisation or AI claim about this conjecture beyond Lutsko was found, and the searches for lab and AI-tracker announcements returned nothing on it.
competing_reading: One reading says the problem has been settled in its pair-correlation form for two broad classes of integrable systems (3D boxes and the three-particle Sutherland model) in 2026, so its status changed in the window, and that the Lutsko paper's AI declaration makes this an AI-involved result. Against this: each paper proves a restricted statistic for a special family and says the general conjecture is open; the Haldane–Shastry result shows integrable models can fail the Poisson law, so the 'generic' qualifier does real work; and the Lutsko declaration does not say which step, if any, was the tool's.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The Lutsko author's account of which proof steps, if any, ChatGPT originated, given the sentence 'developing and checking preliminary proof strategies'; and any referee report or verification of arXiv 2609.03112. (2) Peer-review outcomes for Kim–Marklof–Welsh and Lutsko, and whether a later survey still calls the generic statement open. (3) The identity and date of the Monk-coauthored result named in the 21 Oct 2025 Oxford talk. (4) The Sarnak 1995 text (year and scope of the almost-every-torus theorem) and VanderKam's original paper. (5) A judgement on whether the 'first rigorous proof ... deterministic quantum Hamiltonian' claim survives comparison with Eskin–Margulis–Mozes and Kim–Marklof–Welsh; this is for the judging pass. (6) Whether the generic qualifier, as the conjecture is stated, excludes the three-particle Sutherland model and the 3D box.

event.what_happened: Wooyeon Kim, Jens Marklof, Matthew Welsh, 'Values of ternary quadratic forms at integers and the Berry–Tabor conjecture for 3-tori', arXiv 2601.03209 (math.NT; also math-ph and math.DS), v1 submitted 6 Jan 2026 by Welsh; 29 pages. No later version and no journal reference found as of 10 Oct 2026. Verifies the Berry–Tabor two-point spectral density (pair correlation measure) for a quantum particle in a three-dimensional box (Dirichlet Laplacian) when the squared side-length ratios are κ-Diophantine for κ close to 1 (Theorem 1.1; abstract example ratios 1, 2^(1/3), 2^(−1/3)). Extends Eskin–Margulis–Mozes (2005) from dimension two. Method: counting values of ternary forms over shrinking intervals, written as an average of a theta function over unipotent orbits; Ratner's measure classification and escape-of-mass estimates; special diagonal (3,3) forms. Introduction: 'there is currently no complete proof of either phenomenon for a single example.'
event.delivers: Poissonian pair-correlation measure of the rescaled eigenvalues of a three-dimensional box whose squared side-length ratios are κ-Diophantine for κ near 1. Two-point statistic only; one quantum particle in a box; the Diophantine ratio class (the authors note the statement fails for all rational length ratios, where the two-point measure diverges).
event.remains: The spacing distribution ('appears to be equally difficult'); triple and higher correlations ('much less understood in the deterministic setting'); boxes outside the Diophantine class; d ≥ 4 (expected under Diophantine conditions, not proved); other integrable systems and the generic statement. The authors say the Diophantine conditions 'are likely not sharp'.
event.direction: Cuts for the conjecture: verifies the Poisson pair-correlation prediction for a restricted class of integrable systems (3D boxes with Diophantine side ratios). Does not establish the generic statement, which the authors say has no complete proof for a single example.

judgement.why: The statement is the Berry–Tabor conjecture for generic integrable quantum systems; any proof of Poisson pair correlation for a restricted class of genuine integrable quantum spectra (2-tori a.e., Diophantine inhomogeneous/rectangular tori, 3D boxes, three-particle Sutherland) is a case, while results on quantum maps, scattering phase shifts, number-theoretic sequences, neighbouring statistics (small gaps, averaged triple correlation bounds), random-side-ratio form factors, the chaotic side (Marklof–Monk) and a non-generic integrable chain (Haldane–Shastry, which problem_asks itself places outside 'generic') are variants. Post-snapshot, Kim–Marklof–Welsh and Lutsko are unreviewed but credible cases by established authors. The close call is Lutsko's AI role: the declaration says ChatGPT was used 'in developing and checking preliminary proof strategies' alongside checking, exposition, bibliography and LaTeX, and does not say any strategy or argument in the final proof came from it; the author claims independent verification of all arguments. That supports at most strategy discussion on preliminary routes, not identified mathematics in the result, so I answered none. The priority dispute is wording only and does not affect scope or credibility.
judgement.doubts: Lutsko's AI role could be read as 'assisted' if 'developing preliminary proof strategies' fed the final reduction; the record cannot tell, and the quote was obtained via a summarising fetch tool. Pre-snapshot verification calls for Sarnak and Marklof II rest on publication venues only partly verified.
